Check small native Cartesian covariance exports using linear basis probes.

A separate native variational evaluator probes every dynamic parameter at the
nominal GNSS epochs. Python forms J P J^T from the full nuisance-marginalized
parameter covariance. This checks output epochs, column order and cross terms;
GTSAM/QR separately validates the native full inverse. It is an engineering
check of the linearized model, not a nonlinear uncertainty-calibration result.

limitations: The basis evaluator shares native design interpolation semantics with the estimator; this validates epochs, column ordering, and cross terms. QR/GTSAM tests separately validate the full inverse.

Current-runtime fully nonlinear finite differences for one development density knot show about 0.027 percent relative discrepancy from the shared low-degree gravity-gradient transition approximation. This is not an exact-derivative or global covariance-calibration claim.
